memo.recommendation_rationale: This transaction is recommended as a PASS due to critical cash conversion degradation, evidenced by Days Sales Outstanding deteriorating 77% [p.10] from 38 [p.10] to 67 days [p.10] while reported earnings grew. Further severe risks include basic operational contradictions in management's materials—which list irrigation simultaneously as existing revenue ($1.2M [p.15] / 19% [p.5] of 2024 [p.18] revenue) and a new growth initiative—and claim limited seasonality despite summer peak revenues ($0.70M [p.10]) reaching more than double winter levels ($0.30M [p.10]). Finally, reported recurring revenue visibility is severely compromised by standard 30-day [p.3] termination for convenience provisions across customer contracts.
memo.business_overview: Founded in 2011 [p.3] and headquartered in Raleigh, North Carolina [p.3], Verdant Grounds Management operates with 96 employees [p.3] providing commercial landscape maintenance, enhancement, irrigation, and seasonal services. Detailed extractions for description, end markets, service lines, revenue model, top customers, and management remain pending review and are not yet established. Based on available disclosures, the business serves commercial real estate, HOA communities, corporate campuses, and retail centers across 126 customers [p.11], reporting 64.0% [p.3] of its total revenue as recurring maintenance contracts.
memo.financial_summary:
Top-line revenue expanded from $5.1 million [p.18] in 2022 [p.18] to $5.7 million [p.18] in 2023 [p.18] and $6.4 million [p.18] in 2024 [p.18], accompanied by gross profit growth from $1.6 million [p.18] to $1.8 million [p.18] and $1.9 million [p.18]. However, earnings quality shows notable divergence between reported and adjusted profitability figures. Reported EBITDA remained flat at $0.6 million [p.18] in 2022 [p.18], $0.7 million [p.18] in 2023 [p.18], and $0.7 million [p.18] in 2024 [p.18], whereas Adjusted EBITDA is presented higher at $0.7 million [p.18] in 2022 [p.18], $0.8 million [p.18] in 2023 [p.18], and $0.9 million [p.9] in 2024 [p.9]. Specific underlying addbacks—including owner personal expenses, equipment write-offs, and transaction preparation—remain pending review.

Earnings quality is further degraded by severe working capital impairment. Days sales outstanding expanded continuously from 38.0 days [p.10] in 2022 [p.10] to 49.5 days [p.10] in 2023 [p.10] and 67.3 days [p.10] in 2024 [p.10]. This 77% [p.10] surge in DSO demonstrates that cash collection is failing to keep pace with recognized revenue, creating potential bad debt exposure or revenue recognition timing gaps that artificially inflate reported EBITDA relative to cash realization.
memo.thesis_commentary: On paper, the business satisfies all screening criteria for the services rollup strategy, achieving pass marks across targeted revenue scale ($6.4 million [p.9]), organic growth, EBITDA margin, entry valuation at an asking multiple of 6.5x [p.18] ($5.6 million [p.18] asking price), customer concentration limits (largest customer at 14.8% [p.11] and top 5 [p.11] accounts at 48.9% [p.11]), and reported recurring revenue at 64.0% [p.3]. However, these pass marks are misleading when interpreted alongside operational red flags. High reported contract visibility (64.0% [p.3]) is undermined by 30-day [p.3] termination provisions, customer concentration compliance relies on single-account thresholds that mask broader account vulnerability, and executive management continuity consists of only 3 [p.13] individuals for a 96-employee [p.3] business. Furthermore, proposed inorganic expansion assumes acquisition capabilities despite management completing 0 [p.4] acquisitions in its 13-year [p.4] history.
